src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:65 `--caused-by=<id> On a bug close, draw a caused_by link to the culprit` — caused_by has an observable edge effect that regression=close does not require, so dropping it still yields status closed
advisory.finding: The `caused-by-bug-close` oracle row asserts only that the bug reached status 'closed', never that the `caused_by` link/edge to the culprit was actually written. A `regression` close does not require `caused_by`, so a library or CLI adapter that silently accepts-but-drops `caused_by` still closes the ticket and passes the oracle — the row cannot detect a dropped-caused_by regression on the non-xfail surfaces.
scenarios: A future refactor or a CLI/library adapter change silently drops the caused_by argument; the bug still closes; the oracle stays green while the culprit edge is never written.

The row uses ref=HEAD on a close with no verification gate, so ref honoring vs. dropping produces the same status for all three adapters
advisory.finding: The `ref-close` oracle row (`inputs={"ref": "HEAD"}`, plain task, no gate) asserts only status=='closed'. On a non-gated close nothing consumes `ref`, so a correctly-threaded ref, a dropped ref, and an ignored ref are all indistinguishable by status on every adapter — the row is effectively vacuous for the ACCEPTED path and cannot detect a ref-handling regression on library/CLI (the very defect scratchy documents for MCP: 'MCP ref selected HEAD instead of the requested older commit').
scenarios: Library or CLI ref threading regresses (or the row's ref is silently ignored); status is still 'closed'; the oracle passes without ever exercising ref-specific behavior.
